key_insight: ClinPRISM makes irregular clinical time-series question answering practical by compressing sparse, asynchronous observations into a small set of LLM-friendly tokens without sacrificing accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework is designed for efficient healthcare deployment, combining multimodal reasoning with low token usage and fast inference for cost-effective clinical QA.
method: Irregularity-aware multi-scale encoder captures sparse clinical evidence across multiple temporal resolutions.
Temporal evidence distiller merges multi-scale signals into a compact token set compatible with the LLM.
Progressive alignment gradually maps irregular trajectories into the LLM textual embedding space.
evidence_signal: The authors trained on 30,000 clinical time series with multi-scale descriptions and 41,000 instruction-tuning instances across 11 tasks, and report state-of-the-art results with only 16 time-series tokens and 0.15 s average inference latency per question.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of irregular clinical annotations, and the compact token budget could limit fidelity for highly complex trajectories.
paper_title: A Cost-Effective Multimodal LLM Reasoning Framework for Question Answering over Irregular Clinical Time Series
